sentences.text: A string of technology outages has disrupted email, air travel and banking across the United States.
sentences.soundNote: "String of" joins up: the G is soft and "of" is a quick "uv." The stress is on OUT in "outages."

sentences.text: It began on November 12, when Microsoft's email service went down worldwide, and the trouble lasted into the next day.
sentences.soundNote: "Went down" has two strong beats. "Lasted into" links: "las-ti-din-to."

sentences.text: A day later, the FAA, which runs air traffic control, halted takeoffs nationwide.
sentences.soundNote: "FAA" is said letter by letter. "Halted takeoffs" has clear stress on HALT and TAKE.

sentences.text: That Friday afternoon, planes sat idle at airports nationwide under an order called a ground stop.
sentences.soundNote: "Sat idle" — the stress is on I in "idle." "Called a" sounds like "call-duh."

sentences.text: Departures were halted for more than four hours, while thousands of planes already in the air landed safely.
sentences.soundNote: "More than" is quick: "more-thun." "In the air" links smoothly: "in-thee-air."

sentences.text: The FAA says a flood of data overwhelmed its aging communications network, so some radio and radar links became unstable.
sentences.soundNote: "A flood of data" — "of" is weak, like "uh." The stress in "overwhelmed" is on WHELMED.

sentences.text: About 12,000 flights were canceled that day, the FAA says, and some travelers were left stranded at airports overnight.
sentences.soundNote: "Left stranded at" melts together: the T in "left" almost disappears and the D slides into "at" — "lef-STRAN-di-dat."

sentences.text: Early findings point to two sites, including a remote one in Arkansas where a new router was being installed.
sentences.soundNote: "Point to two" has three T sounds close together. "Was being installed" is quick and even.

sentences.text: The root cause remains unclear, and the FAA has paused installation of that type of router.
sentences.soundNote: "Type of router" runs together fast. It sounds like "TY-puv router."

sentences.text: A software bug at JPMorgan Chase, the nation's largest bank, delayed transactions, including payments to and from other banks.
sentences.soundNote: "To and from" — "to" and "and" are short and weak, and "from" gets the beat.

sentences.text: And a day after that, several Apple services and a classified network at the National Security Agency were disrupted.
sentences.soundNote: "A day after that" — "after" links to "that" with a soft T. "Classified" has the stress on CLASS.

sentences.text: There's no evidence these events are linked, and none appears to be the result of a cyberattack.
sentences.soundNote: "Result of a" links into one smooth run: "ri-ZUL-tuh-vuh." "There's" is short for "there is."

vocab.meaning: several similar things that happen one after another
vocab.example: The team has had a string of wins this month.

vocab.meaning: a period when a service like power or the internet stops working
vocab.example: The storm caused a power outage across the town.

vocab.meaning: (of a system or website) to stop working for a while
vocab.example: The ticket website went down minutes after sales began.

vocab.meaning: to make something stop moving or happening
vocab.example: Heavy snow halted train service for the morning.

vocab.meaning: to stay in one place without being used
vocab.example: The machines sat idle while the factory waited for parts.

vocab.meaning: an official order that keeps planes from taking off
vocab.example: A ground stop kept every flight at the gate for an hour.

vocab.meaning: to be too much for a person or system to handle
vocab.example: Calls from worried customers overwhelmed the help desk.

vocab.meaning: getting old and no longer working as well as before
vocab.example: The city plans to replace its aging water pipes.

vocab.meaning: stuck in a place with no way to leave
vocab.example: The canceled ferry left tourists stranded on the island.

vocab.meaning: to show that something is probably the cause or the answer
vocab.example: The test results point to a problem with the battery.

vocab.meaning: the main, original reason that a problem happened
vocab.example: Engineers are still looking for the root cause of the leak.

vocab.meaning: is still not known or understood
vocab.example: It remains unclear when the bridge will reopen.

vocab.meaning: a mistake in a computer program that makes it work wrongly
vocab.example: A software bug showed the wrong prices in the app.

vocab.meaning: acts of paying, sending or receiving money
vocab.example: The shop handles hundreds of card transactions a day.

vocab.meaning: officially secret and open only to certain people
vocab.example: The report is classified, so reporters cannot read it.

vocab.meaning: connected to each other in some way
vocab.example: Doctors say the two illnesses are not linked.

vocab.meaning: an attempt to break into or damage computer systems
vocab.example: The hospital shut down its network after a cyberattack.

moreFromEmily.note: "An" links to "order," so you hear a small N at the start of "order."
